## Current state

On `main`:

```
R CMD check  — Status: 1 ERROR
BiocCheck    — 2 ERRORS · 2 WARNINGS · 13 NOTES
              (+ 1 transient ERROR — Bioc support-site HTTP 502)
```

The transient ERROR (`Unable to find your email in the Support Site: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway`) is a `bioconductor.org` server issue, not a package issue; it may or may not appear on any given run. PR \#199 addresses the `R CMD CHECK` ERROR and three `BiocCheck` NOTEs (`BugReports:` field added, vignette chunk labels added, `\dontrun{}` → `\donttest{}` in `man/sceptre-package.Rd`). 

**Post-#199 state:**

```
R CMD check  — Status: OK
BiocCheck    — 2 ERRORS · 2 WARNINGS · 10 NOTES
```

Below is a worklist for getting `sceptre` to a clean Bioconductor submission. Items are grouped by **priority level**:

- **(A)** Currently flagged by an automated check (`R CMD check` or `BiocCheck` with `new-package = TRUE`). Concrete rules — the check fails until the item is closed.
- **(B)** Not flagged automatically, but a human reviewer is very likely to raise. Correctness, architecture, or ecosystem-integration concerns. Closing these avoids re-submission rounds.
- **(C)** Not flagged automatically and reviewers may or may not notice. Cleanup and polish — worth doing before submission, but not blocking.

## (A) Automated-check findings

Items currently flagged by `R CMD check` or `BiocCheck`. Severity follows the tool. Each item is annotated with **status** — open, closed by PR #199, or blocked on a downstream decision.

### ERRORs

#### A1 — `Remotes: github::timothy-barry/ondisc` (BiocCheck) {#a1}

Bioc and CRAN don't honour `Remotes:`. Beyond removing the field, every package in `Imports`/`Depends`/`Suggests` must be on CRAN or Bioc — so we also need to resolve `ondisc`'s status. The two main options are:

- **Push `ondisc` to Bioc** — If we want to maintain `ondisc` for usage outside of `sceptre`.
- **Absorb into `sceptre`** — If we don't want to maintain `ondisc` separately. We could keep an unmaintained standalone version of `ondisc` on GitHub for any folks who use it for non-`sceptre` purposes.

Status: **open.**

#### A2 — Package version not `x.99.z` (BiocCheck) {#a2}

Bioc requires new submissions to be at version `0.99.z`. Currently `0.10.3`.

Mechanical fix: bump `Version:` in `DESCRIPTION` once the rest of the submission work is ready. Doing it earlier doesn't hurt but signals "submitting now" to anyone reading the repo. Status: **open.**

#### A3 — Test failures from ggplot2 4.0 / cowplot 1.2.0 (R CMD check)

Eight tests in `tests/testthat/test-plotting_functions.R` (lines 82, 83, 84, 120, 121, 141, 142, 149) fail because cowplot 1.2.0 changed the `$labels` accessor pattern and ggplot2 4.0 deprecated `geom_violin(draw_quantiles = ...)`. Status: **closed by PR #199.**

### WARNINGs

#### A4 — `set.seed()` in package code, 5 sites (BiocCheck) {#a4}

`R/aux_functions.R:90`, `R/assign_grna_functions.R:179`, `R/mixture_model_functs.R:102`, `R/plotting_functions.R:838, :1009`. Bioc rule: package code should not mutate the user's RNG state.

Fix: replace with `withr::with_seed()` or accept seed as an argument. The two plot-body calls are also a latent correctness bug — they corrupt the user's RNG mid-plot.

Sequencing: gated on the C++ RNG decision ([B1](#b1)) since both touch RNG behaviour. Status: **open.**

#### A5 — No Bioconductor software dependencies (BiocCheck) {#a5}

Bioc nudges packages with no Bioc deps to consider CRAN instead. If we absorb `ondisc` into `sceptre`, this will be resolved, as `Rhdf5lib` is a Bioconductor package.

Status: **open.**

## (B) Things human reviewers are very likely to flag

Not in `BiocCheck`, but consistently come up in Bioc review either by reading the code, running examples, or expecting Bioc-ecosystem integration.

### B1 — C++ samplers ignore `set.seed()` {#b1}

The highest-priority B item — a correctness bug, not a style nit.

Every sampler in `src/generate_samples_functions.cpp:36, 78, 140, 164` and `src/negative_control_functions.cpp:37, 112` hardcodes the MT19937 seed to the literal integer `4`. R-side `set.seed()` is silently ignored. Two consequences a reviewer will hit:

- Two consecutive `run_calibration_check()` calls in the same session produce **identical** null draws (same hardcoded seed each time). Anyone exercising the calibration check twice will notice.
- A reviewer who tries `set.seed(42)`, runs, sets the seed again, and gets a different result will flag it.

Resolution options:

- *A.* Route the C++ RNG through R's RNG via `unif_rand()`. Cleanest; behavioural change.
- *B.* Add a `seed = NULL` argument to public functions; default to a draw from R's RNG. Preserves the C++ inner-loop purity.
- *C.* Document the current behaviour as-is. Lowest cost; will draw a reviewer comment.

Lean: **B**. Explicit, testable, makes the seed part of the contract. `NEWS.md` note required.

### B2 — `SingleCellExperiment` integration

The most predictable Bioc-review pushback for any single-cell package: *"Why aren't you using `SingleCellExperiment`?"* However, Kasper is willing to advocate for Bioconductor to overlook this.

### B3 — Missing `setValidity()` on `sceptre_object`

A 41-slot S4 class with no validity method draws a comment. Add cheap invariants: matching matrix dims, valid factor levels for `moi`, integer columns where required.

### B4 — Class-level documentation missing

No `man/sceptre_object-class.Rd`. Reviewers will ask. Add per-slot `@slot` documentation while we're there.

### B5 — `ondisc:::` reaching into private API

Even after gating with `requireNamespace`, the eight `:::` calls into `ondisc`'s unexported internals will draw a fragility comment. Resolution: ondisc adds public wrappers (paired with the minimal path of [A1](#a1)), or absorption (the absorb path of [A1](#a1)) makes this moot.

### B6 — Vignette portability

`vignettes/sceptre.Rmd:34, 381-384, 390` writes to `~/sceptre_outputs` and shells out to `system("rm -rf …")`. Replace with `tempdir()`. Reviewers read vignettes carefully and **will** flag both — the home-dir write is a portability issue, the `rm -rf` is a what-on-earth issue.

### B7 — No Windows CI

The Bioc check farm runs Linux + macOS + **Windows**. `.github/workflows/check-standard.yaml` runs Linux + macOS only. The issues that need to be fixed for Windows are likely (a) incompatibility of multi-core parallelization and (b) filepaths. Once these issues are fixed, add a Windows runner before submission.

### B8 — 0% test coverage on importer / on-disk paths

`R/ondisc_functs.R` (0%), `R/pair_constructor_functs.R` (0%), `R/import_functs.R` (16.6%), `R/getters_and_setters.R` (20.7%). Reviewers don't always run `covr`, but they often do — and they sometimes notice when an entire feature has no tests. Closing all of this before submission is unrealistic; closing **importer** tests is achievable and signals intent.

### B9 — `_v2` / `_v3` / `_v4` naming scars in the public C++ API

`run_low_level_test_full_v4`, `compute_nt_nonzero_matrix_and_n_ok_pairs_v3`, `sample_undercover_pairs_v2` and others survived into the public C++ API. A reviewer skimming function names will ask "which version is current and why are old ones still around?" Defensible v0.99.0 minimum: rename internal ones now; keep deprecation aliases on the public ones.
